description: OSPF Neighbor FSM Conformance Engine per RFC 2328

NeighborFSM.description: Represents a single OSPF neighbor finite state machine instance

constructor_params.neighbor_id: str - identifier for the neighbor router
constructor_params.is_dr: bool - True if this router is DR on the shared network (default False)
constructor_params.is_bdr: bool - True if this router is BDR (default False)
constructor_params.neighbor_is_dr: bool - True if the neighbor is DR (default False)
constructor_params.neighbor_is_bdr: bool - True if the neighbor is BDR (default False)

attributes.state: str - current FSM state, initialized to 'Down'
attributes.is_dr: bool - mutable, updated when DR election changes

process_event.description: Process an FSM event. Returns tuple (old_state, new_state). If the event causes no state change, new_state equals old_state.

params.event: str - one of the 13 FSM events from Section 10.2
params.ls_request_list_empty: bool or None - required context for ExchangeDone event (default None)

OSPFNetwork.description: Manages network topology, DR/BDR roles, and processes event traces

constructor_params.topology_file: str - path to topology JSON file

process_trace.description: Process an event trace file. Creates fresh FSM instances per trace (traces are independent). If an event includes a 'dr_update' field, update the network DR/BDR and FSM role properties BEFORE processing the event.

params.trace_file: str - path to trace JSON file containing 'events' array

validate_transitions.description: Validate claimed state transitions against RFC spec. For each transition, create a temporary FSM in the claimed from_state with appropriate network context, process the event, and check whether the to_state matches. DR updates in the trace are applied cumulatively. Returns list of violations.

params.trace_file: str - path to trace JSON file containing 'transitions' array with from_state and to_state fields

returns.index: int - 0-based index of the violating transition

trace_event_format.event: str - FSM event name from Section 10.2

dr_update.dr: str - new DR router ID for the shared network
dr_update.bdr: str - new BDR router ID for the shared network
dr_update._note: Optional. When present, the network's DR/BDR must be updated and FSM role properties refreshed before processing the event.
